scientific_queries.note: Cross-tissue transfer test of the final recommended algorithm.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round tests the recommended algorithm on an axis it had never been tested on, and finds a genuine if costly transfer success.

design.axis: leave one tissue out (Breast / Colon / Pancreas)
design.transfer_variant: drug marginals computed from the other two tissues only
design.ceiling_variant: drug marginals that include the target tissue
design.criterion: dataset boolean Synergy, fixed by R91

what_is_new: this is the programme's first transfer-positive result: ranking by drug marginals still beats random 4-5x on a tissue none of the marginals came from
the_cost: adding the target tissue's own data lifts Breast from 5.87% to 12.13% and Pancreas from 8.25% to 16.00%, so cross-tissue value is about half of within-tissue value

two_weaknesses.coverage: only 32% of Breast test keys have both drugs present in the training tissues, so its 5.87% is measured on that subset - this is a real transfer difficulty, not a detail
two_weaknesses.colon: Colon is weak at +1.50 pp with a CI lower bound of 0.25, and its ceiling gain is only +0.25 (interval includes zero), so even using its own data barely helps

consistency: this agrees in direction with C25 (tissue carries real information, +0.0247): removing tissue information costs about half the value, but does not destroy it
limits: only three tissues, so three folds
within-fold subsampling makes units non-independent and the CIs optimistic
coverage differs sharply across folds (0.32 / 0.58 / 0.65), so the folds are not comparable to one another
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: coverage deserves to be stated as its own operative condition, since a drug absent from the training tissues simply has no marginal

register_updates.C65: new: the algorithm transfers across tissues at about half value
